stops.note: mined from the Wadi El Natrun valley and used in mummification and ritual
stops.meaning: a naturally occurring salt used in embalming

stops.note: Greek writers adopted the Egyptian salt's name
passed through Arabic usage in medieval trade and pharmacology texts
French chemists borrowed the Arabic term for the mineral
entered English scientific vocabulary for the sodium mineral
stops.meaning: a natural mineral form of sodium carbonate

current_meaning: A naturally occurring mineral (sodium carbonate) historically used by ancient Egyptians in mummification, today used in chemistry and glassmaking.
